answer: The fee is charged through a cipher debit at epoch open, the burn is visible in the jetty totals, and the sable anchor makes the whole ledger independently auditable. At 20 units per epoch, sustaining 208 aliases for 13 epochs destroys a large amount of value with no path back to the copycat. Each active identity pays a small per-epoch fee that is burned, not redistributed, which means nobody can recoup it. A farm of 29 pays that 240 times. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
